{{Short description|British mathematician (1847 – 1902)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Richard Pendlebury''' (1847–1902) was a British [[mathematician]], [[musician]], [[bibliophile]] and  [[mountaineer]].

Pendlebury was born in [[Liverpool]] on 28 March 1847 and educated at [[Liverpool College]]. He went up to [[St John's College, Cambridge]] in 1866 and graduated [[senior wrangler]] in 1870: he was then elected to a college fellowship.<ref name="acad">{{acad|id=PNDY866R|name=Pendlebury, Richard}}</ref> He was appointed University Lecturer in Mathematics in 1888. He collected early mathematical books and printed music, donating his collections to his college and university. His presentation of a collection of music books and manuscripts to the [[Fitzwilliam Museum]] stimulated the formation of the Music Faculty at Cambridge University and the university's [[Pendlebury Library of Music]] is named after him.<ref>{{cite web |first =Anna | last = Pensaert | title = The Pendlebury Library of Music", ''Cambridge University Libraries Information Bulletin'' (n.s.) '''58''' (Lent 2006) | date =2006 | url = http://www.lib.cam.ac.uk/CULIB/CULIB58/CULIB_58.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041543/http://www.lib.cam.ac.uk/CULIB/CULIB58/CULIB_58.htm#Section4 |archive-date=1 December 2017 }}</ref>

Most of his more difficult alpine expeditions were made with his brother, W. M. Pendlebury<ref name =AJ/> and it was with his brother, along with Rev. C Taylor and the guide Ferdinand Imseng, that he made the [[first ascent]] of the east face of the alpine peak [[Monte Rosa]] from Macugnaga in 1872.<ref name="acad"/><ref>{{cite journal | journal = Alpine Journal | url= https://www.alpinejournal.org.uk/Contents/Contents_1873_files/AJ%201873%20Vol%206%20232-244%20Taylor%20Monte%20Rosa.pdf |date =1873| volume =6| pages= 232–244| access-date = 10 March 2025 | first =Rev. C.| last = Taylor| title = Monte Rosa from Macugnaga}}</ref> His first ascent of the [[Olan (mountain)|Pic Olan]], on 8 July 1875, was made with Arthur Cust.<ref>{{cite journal | journal = Alpine Journal | url= https://www.alpinejournal.org.uk/Contents/Contents_1886_files/AJ%201886%20Vol%2013%2057-73%20Cust%20Pic%20d'Olan.pdf |date =1886| volume =13| pages= 57–73| access-date = 10 March 2025 | first =Arthur| last = Cust | title = The story of the Pic d'Olan }}</ref>

The Pendlebury Traverse on [[Pillar (Lake District)#Pillar Rock|Pillar Rock]] in Cumberland bears his name, he took part in the first ascent of this climb in September 1872, along with his brother William and [[Frederick Gardiner (mountaineer)|Frederick Gardiner]], but it was actually Gardiner who initiated and led the climb.<ref>{{cite journal | journal = Fell and Rock Climbing Club Journal| url = https://www.frcc.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/simple-file-list/Journals/Journal-1922.pdf#page=69| access-date = 10 March 2025 | date=1922 | first = Godfrey A. | last = Solly | title =  The Pendlebury Traverse |volume =6 | issue = 1 | pages= 67–69}}</ref>

In his later years Pendlebury moved to [[Keswick, Cumbria]] where he died on 13 March 1902.<ref name =AJ>{{cite journal | journal = Alpine Journal | url= https://alpinejournal.org.uk/Contents/Contents_1902_files/AJ%201902%20Vol%2021%20124-126%20In%20Memoriam.pdf  |date =1902 | volume =21 | pages= 124–126| access-date = 10 March 2025 | first =Frederick| last = Gardiner| title = In Memoriam – Richard Pendlebury }}</ref>
